decisions.reason: 고시생 denotes a state-exam aspirant; 'preparing for the civil service exam' renders it plainly and reads better than the vague, stiff 'exam candidate.'
Splits the run-on into two natural sentences; 'always bragging about how much he knew about IT' conveys 입버릇처럼 말하던 without the clunky 'I remembered how he was always going on.'
'I'm telling you' captures the emphasis of 쓰레기라니까 and makes the retort more colloquial than 'I said it's garbage.'
'Not even a moment's hesitation' is the idiomatic phrasing; 'a hint of hesitation' is flatter.
'wondering how much I could get' and 'verdict came as a serious blow' read more naturally than 'thinking about how much I could get' / 'the blow hit me hard,' with no meaning change.
'grave misunderstanding' fits Jinho's mock-solemn register better than 'serious misunderstanding'; both render 큰 오해 faithfully.
'One look is enough to tell it's shit' is a punchier equivalent of 딱 보기에도 똥이거든, matching the joke's timing better than the trailing clause.
'I wasn't fishing for praise' is idiomatic and concise; SOL's 'I didn't say it because I wanted your praise' is wordier with no fidelity gain.
'making Jinho flinch' preserves the causal 려자 link, and 'behind a desk' avoids BASE's unsupported 'hunched over.'
'constitutes assault on a civilian' fixes BASE's ungrammatical 'falls under assault of a civilian'; 되새기다 is acceptably rendered by 'reflect on.'
'Watching him make such a fuss, I could only sigh' is more direct than SOL's abstract, noun-heavy 'His theatrics drew a sigh from me' and avoids adding performative nuance to 호들갑.
'lowered' better matches 스르륵 내려갔다 (a smooth, gradual descent) than 'dropped,' which implies suddenness.
'Good thinking' is closer to 잘 생각했다 and equally natural; 'Good decision' adds a choice framing the Korean does not.
잘렸어 states the firing explicitly; BASE's blunt 'I already got fired' is faithful, while SOL's elided 'I already did' is vaguer than the source.
'as soon as I got to work' matches 출근하자마자 more precisely than 'the moment I showed up,' and the two-beat delivery suits the beat.
BASE preserves 선택한 (chosen) and 아버지 대신 (in place of my late father); SOL drops 'chosen' and shifts 대신 to unsupported 'With my father gone.'
'how hard I'd worked' and 'The money I earned had paid for' flow better than the stiffer 'having worked hard' / 'With what I earned,' with identical meaning.
'told me I was fired' suits the conversational narration better than 'informed me of my dismissal,' which is stiffly formal for this voice.
피식 웃음 is a short, stifled laugh, not a snort (코웃음); BASE's 'short laugh' is the accurate rendering.
'kind of' is the natural spoken equivalent of 좀 그렇지; 'a little' is equivalent but no improvement.
'Listen to that mouth' is idiomatic and captures 말하는 싸가지, whereas BASE's 'the disrespect on you' is awkward Korean-shaped English.
'Despite his words' and 'follow him out' read more smoothly and track 말은 그렇게 하면서도 / 나오라며 more closely.
'boundary between worlds' and 'Step inside, though, and you'll find it' are idiomatic and match the two-world framing the next sentences establish.
고블린이다 is present-tense general truth; SOL's 'are/can' matches the source's tense while BASE's past tense drifts.
'puking his guts out' captures the violent, comic force of 토악질을 해 대는 better than the neutral 'vomiting.'
'get a grip' is the natural spoken form of 정신 좀 차려, and the period after 'Hey' suits the exasperated beat.
SOL's 'Never mind' is an addition not in 그냥 하시던 일 계속 하세요; BASE's '…Just carry on' stays faithful.
'this was the result' and 'drenched' read more naturally than the awkward 'dead-drunk man' / 'soaked through,' with the same content.
'came standard / the optional extra' sharply renders 기본이요, 옵션이다, and 'whose mouth it had come from' matches 누구 입에서 흐른 것인지.
'background music' preserves the deliberate comic metaphor 배경음, which BASE flattens to 'in the background.'
오늘 하루의 기억들 is 'memories'; BASE's 'memories of the day' is closer than SOL's 'day's events.'
끝내주는구나 is sarcasm; SOL's '*What a fantastic day.*' lands that irony better than BASE's more neutral 'turning out to be.'
'the crowning achievement' carries the sarcastic superlative of 압권이야 more pointedly than 'the highlight of it all.'
Footnote reference correctly follows the sentence period ('stew.[^2]'); BASE misplaces it inside the punctuation.
고시원이라고 is 'It's the goshiwon'; SOL's 'We're at the goshiwon' is a paraphrase.
모두의 가슴속에 있는 거 = 'is in everyone's heart'; BASE keeps that, while SOL adds an unsupported 'lives' metaphor.
Both render 된장찌개 부분에서 adequately; 'reached the part' is no worse than 'got to the part,' so no gain.
더럽게 찝찝하네 has no 'still'; SOL adds that and shifts 찝찝 to 'filthy,' while BASE's 'gross' is accurate.
코끝 is 'tip of my nose'; SOL's 'beneath my nose' misplaces the source image.
방에는 = 'in my room'; BASE matches, while SOL's 'for me' shifts the location phrasing without gain.
Comma-joined clause matches the source's single sentence; SOL's split is a stylistic wash.
Both render 방이 꽉 찬 것 같다 adequately; SOL's rephrasing offers no concrete improvement.
도로 갖다 버려 = 'take it back and throw it away'; BASE drops 'throw away' and adds 'where I found it,' SOL drops 도로('back').
decisions.replacement: *Should I take it back and throw it away?*

decisions.reason: 'Or I could' matches 아니면; BASE's 'instead' follows from the previous line rather than the source connective.
꽤 쓸 만한 물건 = 'fairly useful thing'; SOL shifts to monetary worth and adds unsupported 'might actually.'
똥 is 'shit' (distinct from earlier 쓰레기/'garbage'), and 고물 is 'junk'; BASE preserves both, SOL blurs them.
'sudden flicker of curiosity' tracks 갑자기 드는 호기심, whereas BASE's 'got the better of me' overstates it.
미련 is lingering attachment, not 'lingering hopes,' and 진호 형의 말 = 'what Jinho had meant,' not the narrower 'why he called it garbage.'
'after all' preserves 역시나, which SOL drops; otherwise equivalent.
'There was only' captures 이 전부 as faithfully as 'Just an,' with no meaningful gain in SOL.
Both render 이런 고물을 adequately; SOL's shortening is neutral churn.
'opened it to the first page' is clearer and less ambiguous than BASE's 'opened to the first page.'
Source reads 'Ark - 2020'; SOL's 'Ark-2020' matches its capitalization, while BASE's all-caps 'ARK-2020' is unsupported stylization.
'my eyes stopped on the manufacturing date' matches 눈동자가 멈춘 곳은 제조일이었다 better than BASE's personified 'the manufacturing date stopped me.'
'would have been making' preserves the progressive 만들고 있었겠어 that BASE's 'would have made' loses.
The standalone date line is a deliberate beat in the Korean; BASE preserves it while SOL folds it into the following sentence.
Both render 생성되었고 adequately; SOL's 'appeared' is no improvement.
'the Awakened' as a class is better English and matches 각성자's collective use than the bare 'Awakened.'
Both convey 이른바; BASE's two-sentence form is as faithful as SOL's em-dash compression, with no gain.
그러니까 말도 안 되는 거지 is neutral on proximity; BASE's 'that's impossible' is as faithful as SOL's 'this is.'
'Sleeping was better than reading' matches 잠이라도 자는 게 낫다 more closely than BASE's 'I might as well sleep.'
'in the bloom of youth at twenty-seven' preserves the humorous 방년 27세 wordplay that BASE flattens to 'a twenty-seven-year-old chair.'
'Sleeping in this thing' retains the 자면 (if I sleep) that BASE's 'Wearing something like this' drops.
완전한 무음의 세계 is 'a world of complete silence'; BASE keeps the 'world' metaphor SOL drops.
생각이었다 simply states 'were thoughts'; SOL's 'came flooding in' adds unsupported intensity.
고액 연봉 직종 = 'highly paid profession,' which BASE matches; SOL's 'well paid' weakens 고액.
'before the crack of dawn' matches 꼭두새벽 better than BASE's plain 'before dawn.'
'leave you short of breath' matches 숨이 턱턱 막힐 (suffocating); BASE's 'take your breath away' wrongly imports the positive English idiom.
'So now I'm one of them' renders 이제 내가 그 꼴이 됐군 as faithfully as SOL's 'And now.'
'on an F-rank Hunter's income' matches F급 헌터의 수입으로는, which BASE's 'for an F-rank Hunter' drops.
Both render 금액을 맞춰 왔지만 adequately; SOL's 'scrape together' is neutral churn.
'My late father suddenly came to mind' matches 문득 …생각났다 more closely than BASE's 'I suddenly thought of.'
사회적으로 인정받다 is social recognition; SOL's 'those around him' narrows it away from the source.
게이트 균열로 인한 몬스터들의 습격 is a noun phrase 'attack caused by a Gate breach'; SOL turns it active and adds 'after.'
BASE keeps 그래도 ('even so') but adds 'believe in me'; SOL fixes the verb but drops 그래도—the repair preserves both.
decisions.replacement: *Even so, I've done my best all this time. Please believe me.*

decisions.reason: BASE keeps 나도 모르게 but drops 몸; SOL keeps 'my body' but drops 나도 모르게—the repair retains both.
decisions.replacement: Maybe the alcohol was finally catching up with me, or maybe it was the memories. Without realizing it, my body went slack and my eyes began to close.

decisions.reason: 쏟아져 내리는 is pouring; BASE's 'wave of sleep pouring over me' keeps that, while SOL's 'drowsiness' drops the image.
파고들다 is 'pierce/penetrate'; BASE's 'pierced my ears' is closer than SOL's neutral 'reached my ears.'
SOL adds the blockquote paragraph break so '…May fortune favor you in battle!' stands as its own line, matching the source's separation; BASE runs it into the previous notice.
